$comment: Single source of truth for 'this publisher SELLS its documents'.
Read by BOTH the hub's C4P validator (scripts/validators/cross-ref-checks.ts)
and the maintenance agent's paid_sources.py, which resolves the hub checkout
and loads this file. It lives in the hub because the hub cannot read the
private repo, but the private repo can read the hub.
pqctoday.com does not advertise or sell access to paid content, but a paid
standard's NAME stays editorially relevant. A row matching one of these hosts
must carry access_type=paid and must never be presented as a download.
Deliberately an allowlist, not a heuristic: 'did the fetch fail?' cannot tell
a paywall from an outage, and guessing wrong in the permanent direction
silently removes a real standard from the catalog.
Keep it conservative — a false positive suppresses a legitimate free download.

knownFreeLookalikes.$comment: Documented rather than merely omitted — both have been mistaken for their commercial namesakes.

freeDespitePaidHost.$comment: Exceptions WITHIN a paid host. IEEE 802.x is free of charge via the IEEE GET Program, so standards.ieee.org alone is too coarse a rule for it.
